label: w/d/0/z/c input mid-original-phase, in sequences starting with j/y/v/g/h/k/r/n/u
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, never at the delimiter or during copy, and mostly at t=3..7 (peak t=4-5). It needs the current input to be one of a few tokens: w (36% of mass), d (26%), 0 (17%), z (10%) or c (8%); f fires weakly and other tokens almost never. Which earlier tokens appeared strongly gates it. It is much more likely to fire when the sequence starts with (or the prefix contains) j, y, v, g, h, k, r, n or u, and it is suppressed when the prefix contains tokens like x, f, o, p, b, l, a or e. The top activations (w or d at t=4-6 after prefixes like g y v u, j u y u) fit this. The history effect looks graded and additive, more like a weighted sum over the prefix than a single rule, so boolean predicates top out near F1 0.54 on dev. It mostly fires on first occurrences of the token (91% of mass).
